title: Nicholasville Takes Shape
summary: After Jessamine County split from Fayette in December 1798, Methodist minister Rev. John Metcalf surveyed the Nicholasville town site.
bodyMarkdown:
[Nicholasville](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nicholasville,_Kentucky) was laid out as a county seat. [Jessamine County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Jessamine_County,_Kentucky) was formed from part of Fayette County in December 1798, the 36th county in Kentucky. Sources differ on the exact date: [one account](https://grokipedia.com/page/Jessamine_County,_Kentucky) gives December 19, while [another](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nicholasville,_Kentucky) gives December 17.

The county took its name from Jessamine Creek. Legislator Colonel John Price [proposed](https://grokipedia.com/page/Jessamine_County,_Kentucky) the name after the jessamine flower, which grew widely in the area. A competing local legend gives a different origin for the creek's name.

## A minister's survey

The Reverend John Metcalf, a Methodist minister, surveyed the town site on September 16, 1798. The town was officially laid out on August 26, 1799, on land owned by Thomas Caldwell and Chesley Gates. Metcalf had already founded Bethel Academy in 1794, described as the region's first school, and he organized the first Methodist Episcopal church in 1799.

The county's first court met on February 25, 1799, at the house of Fisher Rice. The choice of Nicholasville as the county seat was confirmed on April 22, 1799. The town's early growth [centered](https://grokipedia.com/page/Nicholasville,_Kentucky) on that role as the seat of government.

Other settlers were already there. Benjamin Netherland, who arrived soon after 1782, built Mingo Tavern in 1793 as a stop for travelers. When a post office opened in October 1801, he became the first postmaster and served until 1822.

## The man behind the name

The town was named for Colonel [George Nicholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Nicholas_(politician)), born about 1754 in Williamsburg, Virginia. He helped write Kentucky's first constitution in 1792 and became the first law professor at Transylvania University. He also briefly served as Kentucky's attorney general.

Nicholas had moved to Lexington after helping Virginia ratify the federal Constitution in 1788. Like many Virginia leaders of his day, he was also an enslaver. The 1787 Virginia tax list shows him holding 27 enslaved adults and 16 enslaved children. He died in Lexington on July 25, 1799, a month before the town bearing his name was laid out.

## Growth

By 1800, Jessamine County had 5,461 people. The town received legislative charters in 1812 and 1823, and its first courthouse was finished in 1823. Farms in the area grew hemp, tobacco, corn and livestock, and hemp processing became a major local industry.

## Kentucky today

Nicholasville is still the seat of Jessamine County, about 12 miles south of Lexington. Its population was 32,036 as of July 1, 2023, and it has ranked as Kentucky's seventh fastest-growing city. The town Metcalf surveyed still carries the name of a constitution writer who died weeks before it was laid out.
